<reason>PRO won the debate's controlling clash: the motion as written condemns systems that tie access to work status, and every employer system CON praised (Germany, Japan, Netherlands) severed exactly that tie by law, while CON's own concession [A2.6] admitted no well-designed system asks a sick worker to job-shop. CON's save — "what German law unties is continuity, not financing" [A4.1] — was quoted back in PRO's closing as the decision rule ("continuity is access"). CON argued skillfully on the narrower payer-vs-funds question (monopoly queues, austerity-exposed budgets, earmarked payroll insulation, the sharp "floor vs. payer" inversion), but that required swapping the motion's comparator for a redesigned one, and CON never defended any system that actually ties access to work status. PRO also escaped CON's sharpest dilemma [A3.2] with the floor/speed distinction [B4.4], which was consistent with their opening's basic-coverage scope. PRO's clipped Rebuttal 2 is a minor execution cost — the substance (A1, A2, weighing) survived and the closing recovered the cut line. Both sides were grounded and disciplined; PRO simply made the debate easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 1 [B2.1-B2.2]: "That is not a rebuttal of the motion. That is the motion." It converted CON's best examples into concessions, framed every later round, and was sealed when PRO's closing quoted CON's own continuity/financing admission as the deciding sentence.</best_rebuttal>
